subject: ventures/uk-sole-trader-vs-limited-company-calculator
professional: a UK chartered accountant (ACCA/ICAEW) advising sole traders on incorporation. First checks: are the 2026/27 rUK income tax bands, personal allowance taper (on adjusted net income, dividends included), Class 4 NIC, Class 1 employee/employer NIC (15% over £5,000, Employment Allowance £10,500), corporation tax 19%/25% with 3/200 marginal relief, the £500 dividend allowance and the 10.75%/35.75%/39.35% dividend rates right; is the director salary taxed with the allowance that is left after dividends; is the State Pension qualifying salary the current lower earnings limit; is the MTD trigger on qualifying (gross) income

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with an independent implementation I wrote from the HMRC 2026/27 rules (scratchpad/uk/indep.mjs: PA 12,570 tapered £1 per £2 of adjusted net income over £100,000, bands 37,700/125,140 on taxable income, £500 dividend nil-rate band using band space, dividend 10.75/35.75/39.35 per GOV.UK 'Tax on dividends' via web search, Class 4 6%/2%, Class 1 8%/2% and 15% over £5,000, CT 19%/25% MR 3/200). Passes: sole trader £80,000 (IT 19,432, Class 4 2,856.60, keep 57,711.40) and £110,000 (IT 33,432 with PA 7,570, Class 4 3,456.60) match to the penny; company £60,000 profit, £12,570 salary, £1,200 costs (employer NI 1,135.50, CT 8,567.96, dividends 36,526.55, dividend tax 3,872.85, keep 45,223.69) match; CT £100,000 = 22,750 matches. Fail: whenever salary + dividends exceed £100,000 the tool taxes the salary with a full personal allowance (calc.mjs:127 incomeTax(salary) ignores dividends), so company take-home is overstated by £5,028 at £150,000, £200,000 and £300,000 profit (200k, best salary 100,000: tool 110,140.99, correct 105,112.99; income tax 27,432 vs 32,460). The salary optimiser picks its salary on these wrong numbers. The lower earnings limit is the 2025/26 £6,500; HMRC 'Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027' gives £6,708 (£129/week).
evidence.completeness: node --test '*.test.mjs': 34 pass. Claimed features walked with node -e against calc.mjs: take-home both ways, best salary search (works, respects salary + employer NI <= profit after costs), every tax line, profit-level table (10 levels + yours), findings (MTD, LEL, taper, dividends, retention), custom salary with refusal when unaffordable, retained profit, summary text and download, Employment Allowance toggle, pension-year toggle. No TODOs or stubs. Served copy via node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin (live host 403 through the proxy).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 34 tests, 0 fail, 0.15 s. Six seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (taper /2 -> /3, MR fraction 3/200 -> 3/250, MTD threshold 50k -> 60k, PA-for-dividends zeroed), 2 survived (dividend additional-rate threshold moved +£10,000; employee NI 2% above UEL set to 0). No test covers a company case whose total income crosses £100,000, which is where the high defect sits; tests are hand-calculations by the author at the low end.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (236 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html. Pure functions, input rejected with messages rather than clamped, salary search constrained by affordability with a regression test. Weaknesses: incomeTax and dividendTax compute the personal allowance on different bases (salary alone vs salary+dividends), the root of the high defect; very long single-line statements (calc.mjs:187, 203, 208-216); comment block above maxAffordableSalary describes bestSalary (calc.mjs:137-141); Employment Allowance credited in full against the director's NI only.
evidence.claims: Backed: dividend 10.75/35.75/39.35 with £500 allowance (GOV.UK via search), employer NI 15% over £5,000, Class 4 6/2, CT 19/25 with MR, £50,000 example 40,268 vs 37,994 (recomputed), £20 gap at £60,000 no costs (tool 20.20), disclaimer (index.html footer 'No warranty', 'Not tax advice'), local-only usage counting of comparison_run/example_loaded/summary_downloaded with opt-out button (usage.mjs, page.test.mjs). Not backed: 'Rates checked against published 2026/27 summaries' while the LEL is 2025/26's £6,500 (calc.mjs:34, index.html:72, calc.mjs:212); 'sole trader keeps more at every profit from £10,000 to £300,000' (index.html FAQ, llms.txt) is contradicted by the tool's own engine at £60,500 with no costs (company +£0.38), and above ~£130k the company figures that support it are themselves overstated by £5,028; the MTD finding fires on profit while its own text says the test is gross income.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an accountant runs a £40k-£100k sole trader through the page, reads the salary, dividend and every tax line, and gets numbers that match an independent computation, with sensible caveats (IR35, director's loan, mortgages). That job is done. For a client at £150k+ profit the company figure is £5,028 too high and the 'best salary' is chosen on wrong numbers, so the advice cannot be used. Not modelled and a practitioner would ask in the first hour: associated companies for the CT limits, pension contributions (disclosed), Scottish bands (disclosed), the MTD test on turnover, Employment Allowance shared with other staff's NI.
evidence.domain: Compared with HMRC 2026/27 rates and the ITA 2007 s.35 taper on adjusted net income: rates, bands, dividend nil-rate band consuming band space, Class 4, Class 1 and CT marginal relief all follow practice. Departs: personal allowance for salary not reduced by dividends; LEL stale (£6,500 vs £6,708), so a £6,600 custom salary gets no warning though the year does not qualify; MTD for ITSA qualifying income is gross trading/property income, not profit (calc.mjs:210); CT limits ignore associated companies and short periods; Class 2 (voluntary below the small profits threshold) not mentioned for low profits.

defects.what: Director salary is taxed with a personal allowance computed on the salary alone (incomeTax(salary)), not on adjusted net income including dividends. Once salary + dividends exceed £100,000 the allowance should taper away; the tool keeps it, so company take-home is overstated by up to £5,028 (150k, 200k, 300k profit) and the best-salary search optimises on the wrong figure (200k: tool 110,140.99 at salary 100,000, correct 105,112.99).

Lower earnings limit is the 2025/26 £6,500; for 2026/27 HMRC sets £6,708 (£129/week). The keep-a-qualifying-year floor, the label 'salary at least £6,500' and the 'below the lower earnings limit' finding all use the stale figure, so a £6,600 salary is presented as protecting a State Pension year when it does not.

Making Tax Digital finding is triggered by profit > £50,000, but MTD qualifying income is gross income before expenses (as the finding's own text says). A sole trader with £45k profit on £70k turnover is told MTD 'will reach' them later when it applies from April 2026.

2 of 6 seeded mutants survive (dividend additional-rate threshold moved £10,000; employee NI 2% above UEL removed); no test covers a company case above £100,000 total income, where the high defect sits.

FAQ and llms.txt say a sole trader keeps more at every profit from £10,000 to £300,000; the tool's own engine gives the company +£0.38 at £60,500 with no costs, and the high-profit end of that claim rests on overstated company figures.

Employment Allowance is credited in full against the director's employer NI only; a company that qualifies because it has other staff uses the allowance against their NI too, so the director's saving is overstated. Corporation tax limits also ignore associated companies.
The comment above maxAffordableSalary describes bestSalary (keepNiYear, lower earnings limit), left behind when the helper was inserted.

verdict: For the page's first visitor (£40k-£100k profit) the numbers are right: sole trader at £80k and £110k, the company at £60k, CT marginal relief at £100k and the £50k headline all match an independent 2026/27 implementation to the penny, and the dividend, NI and CT rates match GOV.UK. It misses the bar on correctness, verification and claims: above about £130k profit the director's salary keeps a personal allowance that dividends have tapered away, overstating company take-home by £5,028 and steering the salary choice; the lower earnings limit is last year's £6,500 (2026/27 is £6,708); the MTD finding tests profit, not gross income; and 2 of 6 seeded mutants survive.
